Estimate group classes with fixed individual profile definitions

Source: R/fixed-measurement.R
fit_staged.Rd

fit_staged() fits a two-level profile model in two stages. The first stage estimates the profiles with one group class; the second holds their measurement parameters (means and covariances of continuous indicators, response probabilities of categorical ones) fixed and estimates the profile probabilities within each group class and the group-class proportions. The profiles therefore keep one definition while the group classes differ in composition. A fitted measurement model can be supplied instead of the first stage, to reuse established profiles. The result holds the second-stage estimates and keeps the first-stage fit.

Information criteria and likelihood-ratio comparisons condition on the held measurement. Staged fits that hold the same measurement are compared on n_parameters. A comparison with a jointly estimated fit uses n_parameters_with_measurement and stays descriptive, since staged estimates do not maximise the joint likelihood. Wald standard errors omit the uncertainty of the first stage. parameter_inference(fit, method = "bootstrap") resamples groups and re-estimates both stages (a supplied same-sample measurement model with its own options), so that uncertainty is propagated and the measurement parameters get intervals too. A measurement fitted to different observations, or with unknown provenance, is refused by this bootstrap; resampling the current data cannot represent uncertainty from an external measurement sample.

Usage

fit_staged(
  data,
  vars,
  id,
  n_profiles,
  n_group_classes = 2L,
  measurement = NULL,
  variance_model = c("varying", "equal"),
  n_starts = 10L,
  max_iter = 1000L,
  tol = 1e-08,
  min_variance = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  missing = c("error", "fiml"),
  covariance_model = c("diagonal", "full"),
  categorical = character(),
  min_probability = 1e-10,
  time = NULL,
  search = NULL,
  n_screen = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with the indicators and the group identifier.

vars

Names of the indicator columns. Those not named in categorical are continuous.

id

Name of the group identifier column (character, factor or numeric, without missing values). Required.

n_profiles

Number of individual profiles.

n_group_classes

Number of group classes in the second stage, at least two (default 2).

measurement

NULL (default) estimates the first stage from data; otherwise a fitted multilpa model supplying the measurement estimates, with one group class and the same profiles, indicators and measurement options. Its covariance structure must be EEI, VVI, EEE or VVV, and it must not have weights, centering, scaling, ordinal or count indicators, direct_effects, local_dependence or noise.

variance_model

"varying" (default): each profile has its own variances or covariance matrix; "equal": one shared by all profiles.

n_starts

Number of EM starts in each estimated stage (default 10). With measurement, only the second stage is estimated.

max_iter

Maximum EM updates per start in each stage (default 1000); zero evaluates the starting values without updating them.

tol

Convergence tolerance (default 1e-8), per observed indicator value: EM stops when a step changes the log likelihood by no more than tol times the number of observed indicator values.

min_variance

Lower bound on every variance (on every covariance eigenvalue under full covariance), as in multilpa(), applied in both stages; a supplied measurement must satisfy it.

seed

Optional integer seed. The caller's random-number state is restored on exit.

missing

"error" (default) rejects missing indicator values; "fiml" maximises the observed-data likelihood under MAR, integrating the missing values out.

covariance_model

"diagonal" (default): the indicators are independent within a profile; "full": within-profile covariances are estimated.

categorical

Indicators modelled by profile-specific response probabilities over their observed categories, the latent class measurement model. Binary, ordered and unordered indicators share this parameterization. Naming a subset of vars fits a mixed-mode model.

min_probability

Lower bound on every categorical response probability (default 1e-10).

time

Optional column giving each row's occasion within its group, used only to order the rows for get_results(x, "sequences"), "sequence_summary" and plot_sequences(). Values must be unique within a group and sort in their intended order (numbers numerically, factors by level, text alphabetically, so "T2", "T10" is refused: use a factor or zero-pad).

search

NULL (default), "kmeans" or "emEM" for each estimated stage, as under multilpa(): the default is "emEM" for continuous indicators with a shared covariance matrix (EEI or EEE) and "kmeans" otherwise. The second stage starts from the first-stage measurement and holds it.

n_screen

For search = "emEM" only, the size of the screened pool (default five times n_starts, at least n_starts). The second stage skips screening when n_starts = 1.

Value

A second-stage multilpa object whose measurement parameters equal the first-stage estimates; fixed names the held blocks, n_parameters counts the second-stage parameters and n_parameters_with_measurement adds the measurement ones. get_results(fit, what = "stages") summarises the two stages in two rows. Every table, plot and diagnostic of a multilpa fit applies.

See also

multilpa() for holding chosen blocks through fixed; starting_values(fit, what = "measurement") to extract measurement parameters for a later fit.

Examples

set.seed(7)
example_data <- data.frame(
  school = rep(seq_len(30), each = 8),
  score_a = stats::rnorm(240), score_b = stats::rnorm(240)
)
staged <- fit_staged(example_data, c("score_a", "score_b"), "school",
                     n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2, n_starts = 2,
                     seed = 1)
get_results(staged, what = "stages")
#>         stage group_classes            fixed log_likelihood parameters
#> 1 measurement             1             <NA>      -671.8928          9
#> 2  membership             2 means, variances      -671.8928          3
#>   parameters_with_measurement converged
#> 1                           9      TRUE
#> 2                          11      TRUE
get_results(staged, what = "profile_probabilities")
#>   group_class profile probability group_class_probability
#> 1           1       1   0.9782787                     0.5
#> 2           1       2   0.0217213                     0.5
#> 3           2       1   0.9782787                     0.5
#> 4           2       2   0.0217213                     0.5
